clinician.trajectory_summary: An 82-year-old male with history of treated pulmonary tuberculosis (20 years prior), COPD, and surgically resected cutaneous melanoma (1 year prior) presented with sudden onset of seizures. MRI brain on admission revealed multiple white matter CNS lesions with peripheral contrast enhancement. CSF analysis showed elevated protein (1103 mg/L) and lactate (2.7 mmol/L) with normal cell count and glucose; cultures and PCR were negative for bacterial, viral, fungal, TB, and Entamoeba pathogens, effectively ruling out infectious etiologies despite positive serum E. histolytica serology. The right frontal CNS lesion was surgically excised en bloc, presenting as a firm, elastic, round, well-capsulated mass with necrotic-like core. Histopathology demonstrated histiocytic granulomatous tissue with IgG4-producing plasma cells (IgG4/IgG ratio 45%, IgG4 >10/HPF), diagnostic for IgG4-related disease. The patient was initiated on high-dose prednisone (1 mg/kg twice daily) with rapid clinical improvement evident after 10 days, achieving independent ambulation with minimal aid by week 2. Total-body CT performed during clinical course showed bilateral bronchiectasis and lung cavitation, likely representing sequelae of prior tuberculosis rather than active IgG4-RD pulmonary involvement.

final.final_diagnosis: IgG4-related disease with CNS involvement presenting as multiple brain lesions
final.trajectory_summary: An 82-year-old male with history of treated pulmonary tuberculosis (20 years prior), COPD, and surgically resected cutaneous melanoma (1 year prior) presented with sudden onset of seizures. MRI brain on admission revealed multiple white matter CNS lesions with peripheral contrast enhancement. CSF analysis showed elevated protein (1103 mg/L) and lactate (2.7 mmol/L) with normal cell count and glucose; cultures and PCR were negative for bacterial, viral, fungal, TB, and Entamoeba pathogens, effectively ruling out infectious etiologies despite positive serum E. histolytica serology. The right frontal CNS lesion was surgically excised en bloc, presenting as a firm, elastic, round, well-capsulated mass with necrotic-like core. Histopathology demonstrated histiocytic granulomatous tissue with IgG4-producing plasma cells (IgG4/IgG ratio 45%, IgG4 >10/HPF), diagnostic for IgG4-related disease. The patient was initiated on high-dose prednisone (1 mg/kg twice daily) with rapid clinical improvement evident after 10 days, achieving independent ambulation with minimal aid by week 2. Total-body CT performed during clinical course showed bilateral bronchiectasis and lung cavitation, likely representing sequelae of prior tuberculosis rather than active IgG4-RD pulmonary involvement.
